messages.subject: release of version 0.3-1 of NIMBLE
messages.body_plain:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,

We're pleased to announce that we've released version 0.3-1 of NIMBLE at
R-nimble.org.

Version 0.3-1 is a minor release with a few additional features and some
bug fixes, all detailed in the NEWS page of the package/Github page and
the NIMBLE website.

These are still early days for NIMBLE.  Please take a moment to let us
know what you're trying to use it for and what would make it better.
You can email the development team directly at nimble...@gmail.com
or share with the nimble-users list at nimble...@googlegroups.com.

 - Chris Paciorek for the NIMBLE Development Team

messages.subject: many nodes not sampled in hierarchical models
messages.subject_clean: many nodes not sampled in hierarchical models
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

NIMBLE seems to work seamlessly and blazingly fast when I have a relatively simple model, but when I try to fit more complex hierarchical models, I tend to always get back many un-sampled nodes. That is, for certain nodes the MCMC chain returns only a single value, or that value is just NaN. Do hierarchical models require more "hands-on" initialization? And, what is the best way to do that (should I 'calculate' and 'simulate' for every node before running the MCMC; is there a wrapper for doing every node)?

Here is an example model (this is not meant to be reproducible, just and example of the type of model I am working with), that when I run only returns non-NaN samples for 'tau'.

Thanks,
Andrew

####
####  Example BUGS code
####

model <- nimbleCode({
  #process model and likelihood
  for(i in 1:nObs){
    mu[i] <- intYr[spp[i],yrs[i]] + intG[spp[i],grp[i]] + beta[spp[i],yrs[i]]*X[i] +
      nb[spp[i]]*crowd[i] + temp1[spp[i]]*TmeanSpr1[i] + rain1[spp[i]]*ppt1[i] +
    tau2[i] <- 1/(tau[spp[i]]*exp(tauSize[spp[i]]*mu[i]))
    tau3[i] <- max(tau2[i],0.00000001)
    Y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau3[spp[i]])
  }

  #priors
  for(s in 1:nSpp){
    tau[s] ~ dnorm(0,0.001)
    tauSize[s] ~ dnorm(0,0.001)
    betaSpp[s] ~ dnorm(0, 1e-6)
    nb[s] ~ dnorm(0, 1e-6)
    temp1[s] ~ dnorm(temp1Mu, temp1Var)
    rain1[s] ~ dnorm(rain1Mu, rain1Var)
    intercept[s] ~ dnorm(0, 1e-6)
    intVaryY[s] ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
    betaVar[s] ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
    intVarG[s] ~ dgamma(2, 0.5)

    for(y in 1:nYrs){
      intYr[s,y] ~ dnorm(intercept[s], intVaryY[s])
      beta[s,y] ~ dnorm(betaSpp[s], betaVar[s])
    }
    for(g in 1:nGrp){
      intG[s,g] ~ dnorm(0, intVarG[s])
    }
  }

  temp1Mu ~ dnorm(0,1e-6)
  rain1Mu ~ dnorm(0,1e-6)
  temp1Var ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
  rain1Var ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
})

messages.subject: Re: many nodes not sampled in hierarchical models
messages.subject_clean: many nodes not sampled in hierarchical models
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew, it's entirely possible something is going wrong on our
side, but a couple comments on your model to first see if all is well
on that side of things.

1) tau3 is a vector of length nObs, but you are indexing into it with
spp[i] in the Y[i] declaration.  Does spp[i] always give a value
between 1 and nObs?
2) your mu[i] line ends in a "+". Presumably just a typo in the email,
as otherwise the code would error out when you try to create the model
in NIMBLE, but can you show the full model?
3) In general, we handle initialization using the prior if initial
values are not given but if you have non-informative priors as you do,
this can give crazy starting values (e.g., for variance components)
and that can lead to numerical issues. So it's good to give reasonable
starting values, particularly for the top-level parameters.

If that doesn't address things, a reproducible example would be great.
